summary: Tower placed in Thunder Bay District by Firelookout.ca and at Marathon by a hobby list, which may be the same tower; a Firelookout.ca note on an October 2025 flyover says it stands without a cupola. Little else documented.

facts.status_note: Still stands with no cupola, per a Firelookout.ca note that describes an October 2025 flyover; the hobby list, dated as of 2013, has no cupola-removal star for it.

events.note: Firelookout.ca note: writer flew directly over the tower in October 2025 and saw it standing with no cupola. An aerial view, not a ground visit.

evidence.supports: Writer was working on the White River in October 2025 and flew directly over the tower
evidence.quote: Was working on the White River in October 2025, and flew directly over the tower.

evidence.supports: Writer unsure how to reach the tower on the ground
evidence.quote: Unsure how you would access it on the ground.

evidence.supports: Old logging trails seen on satellite imagery, now very overgrown; no significant trails nearby
evidence.quote: Did not see any significant trails nearby, however, Google sat view does show some old logging trails (very overgrown now).

evidence.supports: Tower standing with no cupola (directory note)
evidence.quote: Tower is standing with no cupola.

evidence.supports: Listed on the still-standing list as Lecours Tower at Marathon, Ont., with no cupola-removal star
Star legend: a star marks a cupola removal
MNR decided as of 2013 to remove many still-standing towers
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these still standing towers.

evidence.supports: MNR no longer maintains the listed towers; visitors asked not to climb
evidence.quote: The MNR no longer maintains them so please refrain from climbing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The list has no cupola-removal star beside Lecours, while the Firelookout.ca note says there is no cupola. The list is dated as of 2013 and the note describes an October 2025 flyover, so the note is the more recent account.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only, and the 2025 note is an aerial sighting by a directory commenter, not a ground visit. The brief's Thunder Bay District (from Firelookout.ca) and the list's Marathon are not reconciled; no source connects the two. No build date, height, design, staffing or access level found, so none are given. Access is omitted because no source says whether the public may visit. Follow-up: MNR fire records, Marathon-area local history, and Forest History Ontario archives.
